reasoning: The test uses Playwright's APIRequestContext (request.post()) to call /api/people/create, which makes a raw HTTP request outside the browser. The server's CSRF protection (security.py protect_unsafe_request) requires an X-CSRF-Token header for non-safe methods, which the browser normally injects via security.js intercepting window.fetch. Since APIRequestContext bypasses the browser, no CSRF token is sent, and the server returns 403. The face-assignment.spec.ts correctly uses page.evaluate() with window.fetch for the same API endpoints. The spec goals (creating people via the API) are achievable — the test just uses the wrong mechanism to call them.
suggestedAction: Replace the request.post()-based createPersonViaApi and assignFaceToPersonViaApi helpers with page.evaluate()-based implementations that use window.fetch (mirroring the pattern in face-assignment.spec.ts). Change function signatures from (request: APIRequestContext, ...) to (page: Page, ...). Update all call sites accordingly.
